name: Crazy Shit
description: The album where the language gets loose: breaks fed through a shredder, a choir that thinks it is a microwave, a soprano who can only say meow, sines bent into their own harmonics, melodies grown by rewriting rules, the world's fastest polka, five tempos colliding, a swarm of bees inside your skull, a piano melted four different ways and a toaster with opinions. Nothing here is tasteful. Every sketch is a whole piece with a song structure that ends on its own, and every sketch explains its trick in the comments.
author: Claude, for Tartlet

sketches.name: Gremlin Factory
sketches.description: One drum break, scrambled, ratcheted, hurried and bit-crushed differently almost every bar, over a bass ring-modulated into a gargling metal lump and bells that never know their key. The break comes round twice with a different ending each time, then once more backwards.

sketches.name: Microwave Choir
sketches.description: A church choir that thinks it is a kitchen appliance: ring-modulated, frequency-shifted and humming like a turntable, while a robot sings beep boop and the timer dings three times at the end of every section.

sketches.name: Cat Opera
sketches.description: A soprano who can only say meow, gliding three vowels across every note with a dramatic scoop, a tenor tomcat answering from the fence, pizzicato strings in a violin body and a purr underneath. The reprise goes up an octave, as cats do, and the finale slows to a halt.

sketches.name: Chebyshev's Revenge
sketches.description: A plain sine pushed through a different Chebyshev curve each bar, so the tune leaps up the harmonic series, over a bass folded onto itself harder through every section until it tears and drums run through a rectifier. The riff comes round twice, once ending in a fold, once in a rectifier.
sketches.source:
setcpm(96/4)

// The riff twice, ending once on the folded bass alone and once on the rectified drums alone
song("intro@4 (riff@12 1.fold@4 2.rect@4)*2 outro@4", "once")

// A loud sine through chebyN comes out as its Nth harmonic:
// one tune, jumping to the 2nd, 3rd, 5th and 7th harmonic bar by bar
lead: n("0 2 4 7 4 2 0 -1").scale("A:minor").transpose(12)
  .s("sine").curve("<cheby2 cheby3 cheby5 cheby7>").drive(18)
  .decay(.2).sustain(.4).release(.1).lpf(6000).gain(.18)
  .sections("riff outro")

// A bass folded over on itself, harder through every section, through a stack cabinet
bass: note("<a1 a1 f1 g1>").struct("x ~ x x ~ x ~ x").s("sine")
  .curve("fold").drive(env("4 22", "section")).bias(.2)
  .decay(.2).sustain(.4).release(.05).cab("stack").gain(.35)
  .exceptSections("intro rect")

// Drums through a full-wave rectifier, half wet, with a doubled fill on the last bar of each section
drums: s("bd ~ bd ~, ~ sd ~ sd, hh*8").curve("rect").drive(8).curvemix(.5).gain(.45)
  .exceptSections("fold outro").atEnd(1, x => x.ply(2))

sketches.name: Fractal Panic
sketches.description: A melody grown for seven generations of rewriting, in phrygian dominant, over kicks and snares from residue-class sieves, Thue-Morse hats, toms on the primes and a bass counting Collatz steps through a screaming filter. Each number-theory layer gets its own section before they all pile up.
sketches.source:
setcpm(140/4)

// Sieves twice, first answered by Collatz alone, then by everything at once
song("intro@4 (sieve@16 1.collatz@8 2.lsys@8)*2 outro@4", "once")

// Seven generations of rewriting: 0 becomes 0 3, 3 becomes 5 0, 5 becomes 3, spread over four bars
melody: n(lsys("0", "0=0 3, 3=5 0, 5=3", 7, 4)).scale("C:phrygian dominant").transpose(12)
  .s("square").pw(.2).decay(.08).sustain(0).delay(.25).delaytime(3/16).gain(.16)
  .exceptSections("intro collatz")

// Rhythms from number theory, layered until they make no sense
kick: s("bd").struct(sieve("3@0 | 5@1", 16)).shape(.3).gain(.7).exceptSections("outro")
snare: s("sd").struct(sieve("7@3 | 11@6", 16)).gain(.45).sections("sieve lsys")
hats: s("hh").struct(ints("thuemorse", 16)).hpf(7000).gain(.25)
toms: s("lt").struct(ints("prime", 16)).speed(ints("ruler", 16).add(1)).gain(.3)
  .sections("collatz lsys")

// The bass counts Collatz steps from each step number, folded into seven degrees, and screams about it
bass: n(ints("collatz", 4).mod(7)).scale("C:phrygian dominant").octave(-1)
  .s("sawtooth").lpf(900).lpq(12).lpenv(3).lpdecay(.1).decay(.15).sustain(.3).gain(.35)
  .exceptSections("intro outro")

sketches.name: Polka Apocalypse
sketches.description: The world's fastest polka at 220 BPM, which rushes to double speed on the last bar of every section and accelerates into the end of the world, while an air-raid siren wails and a rumble grows louder across the whole piece as the sky falls.

sketches.name: Tempo Soup
sketches.description: One figure at five speeds at once, aligned so they all crash into the same note at the end of every sixteen-bar section, while two drummers who disagree drift apart and meet again, and the whole kitchen slows down to finish.
sketches.source:
setcpm(100/4)

// Three bowls of soup, sixteen bars each, so every convergence lands on a section boundary
song("intro@4 soup@16 soup'@16 soup''@16 outro@4", "once")
tempomap("0:25 52:25 56:18")

// One figure at five speeds, shifted so that every copy reaches the start together at bar 16
soup: n("0 3 5 7 10 7 5 3").scale("C:minor pentatonic").transpose(12)
  .converge(16, 1, 7/6, 5/4, 4/3, 3/2)
  .s("triangle").timbre("glass").decay(.15).sustain(0).pan(rand).room(.4).gain(.1)
  .exceptSections("intro")

// Two drummers who disagree: one holds still, the other slips a sixteenth further every bar
drummer1: s("bd ~ sd ~ bd bd sd ~, hh*8").pan(.3).gain(.4).exceptSections("outro")
drummer2: s("bd ~ sd ~ bd bd sd ~, hh*8").phase(1/16).pan(.7).gain(.35).sections("soup")

// A crash on each meeting point: sections restart at bar zero, so it hits the first bar of each
crash: s("<cr ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~>").room(.6).gain(.4).sections("soup outro")

bass: note("<c2 eb2 f2 g2>").s("sine").shape(.2).decay(.4).sustain(.4).release(.2).gain(.4)

sketches.name: Bees in Your Skull
sketches.description: Headphones on: three insects circling your head at different speeds and heights, hats hopping between your ears in a seeded random order, and a drone whose interaural phase spins faster in every section, staying just below the rates that trigger a pulse warning. Only the kick stays in the middle, and the swarm leaves at the end.

sketches.name: Spectral Meltdown
sketches.description: One innocent piano phrase and four ways to wreck it, eight bars each: played plainly, frozen into a smear, blurred into fog and combed into metal, while the bass is pitch-shifted further each section until it turns into a robot. A plain coda slows to a stop.

sketches.name: Talking Toaster
sketches.description: A kitchen at breakfast: a saw bass that talks in syllables, a radio muttering through a bit-crusher, a kettle working up to a whistle, and at the end a toaster pop and a robot voice announcing that the toast is ready.
